items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: He was at Play Boy Flour for a long time... And that was all completely different from what Bob Wills was playing.

ctx.x: Yeah, Bob Wills. He was at Play Boy Flour for a long time. And he played, well I still called it hillbilly, but it’s different. It’s a different style of music. But I never, along that same time I was playing with my brother-in-law and we’d you know take a song and we’d play the melody out and then after playing the melody I mean I’d play some chords or changes or something like that. And that was all completely different from what Bob Wills was playing.

And about the violin. You know you said in the early days there weren’t that many people who played jazz on the violin. Tell us a little bit about this tour that you did with I think it was four other violinists what they play what they call “Folk Violin.”
